si_4_title: Individualized resting-state functional connectivity abnormalities unveil two major depressive disorder subtypes with contrasting abnormal patterns of abnormality

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: REST-meta-MDD (1276 MDD patients, 1104 healthy controls) was the primary dataset for identifying MDD subtypes. COBRE (72 schizophrenia patients, 74 healthy controls) was used for disease specificity analysis.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: The imaging datasets for MDD used in this study were sourced from the REST-meta-MDD consortium ... we applied the same analysis pipeline to a dataset of schizophrenia patients from Centre for Biomedical Research Excellence (COBRE...)

answer.REST-meta-MDD: primary dataset for constructing normative ranges (tolerance intervals) using HCs and identifying subtypes in MDD patients

answer.COBRE: used for disease specificity analysis to examine if extreme functional connectivity patterns are unique to MDD

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: REST-meta-MDD HCs were used to define normative ranges for MDD patient subtyping. COBRE HCs were used to define normative ranges for SCZ patients to verify disease specificity.

dc_3_hc_number_of_each_normative_model.detail: Model 1 uses 1104 HCs from the REST-meta-MDD consortium. Model 2 uses 74 HCs from the COBRE dataset. The non-parametric tolerance interval approach typically uses the entire HC sample to define the normative range without a separate training/validation split for the HC data itself.
